helpText._0: Unicode names mix traditions: many list the Elder Futhark name with its Anglo-Saxon and Norse names and a letter, such as RUNIC LETTER FEHU FEOH FE F.

A reconstructed Proto-Germanic name, as written in English Wikipedia's Elder Futhark table. No source from the time of the Elder Futhark records the names; they are reconstructed from later rune poems, and some are uncertain.

BGN/PCGN romanization of the letter on its own: ye and yë are the forms at the start of a word or after a vowel (elsewhere e and ë); the hard sign and the soft sign are written ˮ and ʼ and have no sound of their own.
